h1: Hydraulic shears — swing beam and guillotine plate shears, 12 ga to 1-9/16″
intro: A hydraulic shear cuts sheet and plate to size in one stroke between a fixed lower blade and a moving upper blade driven by two hydraulic cylinders; the back gauge sets the width, hydraulic hold-downs keep the sheet flat and the control counts the strokes. It is the shear for plate — from 12 ga to 1-9/16″ and 26 ft here — where tonnage matters more than strokes per minute. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, all on this page: swing beam shears, the rugged everyday plate shear with the beam swung through the cut on two bearings — the premium BS / BSY to 5/8″ over 13.5 ft and the value-line QC12K from 5/32″ to 3/4″ over 20 ft; guillotine shears with a variable rake angle on a beam carried straight down on rollers, so thin sheet is cut flat and 3/4″ plate with less distortion — the premium DAS CNC to 3/4″ × 20 ft with the ESA 630 control and the value-line Q11K to 1-9/16″ × 26 ft; and light hydraulic shears from 12 ga to 1/4″ over 51 – 120″ for the sheet-metal shop. Every model is in the table below with its capacity, length, strokes, motor and weight, then each family with its full specification and photos. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For sheet to 1/4″ all day with no hydraulics, see the mechanical guillotine shears; for 20 – 14 ga, the sheet metal shears.

faq.a: A swing beam shear pivots the upper blade on two bearings and drives it down with two cylinders: a simple, rigid machine with few moving parts, a fixed cutting angle and a slightly curved blade path — the right shear for most fabrication shops cutting 5/32″ to 1/2″ sheet. A guillotine shear carries the blade beam on linear rollers so it comes straight down, and the rake angle is set by the control: thin sheet is cut at 0.5° fast and flat, thick plate at 3° or 4° with less twist and less force — the production machine, and the only choice above 3/4″.

The premium BS / BSY and DAS shears are built by Dener in Turkey with Rexroth or Hoerbiger hydraulics, ESA or Delem controls, the heaviest frames and Dener Canada parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada — the machines for two shifts a day and the tightest, flattest cut, with the DAS CNC setting rake, gap and gauge from the material keyed in. NovoTech's value-line QC12K and Q11K are the same two designs — swing beam and variable-rake guillotine — built in China to our specification with Estun controls, Rexroth hydraulics and Siemens motors at about two-thirds of the price, in more sizes (to 1-9/16″ and 26 ft). Both lines are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians, and the light hydraulic shears below them are the value-line answer for 12 ga to 1/4″.

faq.q: What thickness and length do I need?
faq.a: Capacities are rated for mild steel of 65,000 psi; stainless cuts about 60 % of the rated thickness and aluminum about 150 %. Choose the length from the sheet you buy: 8 ft (2,500 mm) for 4 × 8 sheet cut across, 10 ft (3,200 mm) for 5 × 10 sheet, 13 ft and up for plate. The 1/4″ × 10 ft swing beam shear (QC12K-6×3200) is the Canadian standard; a shop cutting 3/8″ and 1/2″ plate daily should look at the 10 or 13 mm guillotine.

The BS / BSY come with an NC control for the back gauge and the stroke counter; the DAS with the ESA 630 CNC — back gauge, blade gap, cutting angle and stroke length programmed per material, with a parts memory and a 1 m ball-screw back gauge with retract. Delem controls are available on request.

faq.q: What does the Estun E21S control do?
faq.a: It positions the motorised back gauge (0.8 – 25.6″, 31.5″ on the long machines) with a servo, sets the cutting angle and displays the blade clearance from an encoder, counts strokes and stores 40 programs of 25 steps, in inches or millimetres; a retract function pulls the gauge back after the cut so the strip falls free. The E200PS and the Delem DAC-360T add programmable blade-gap adjustment.

faq.q: What is standard on a Dener shear?
faq.a: Hydraulic hold-downs (16 – 33 on the DAS), a squaring arm with scale, front support arms, a ball-transfer table, a shadow-line light, a photocell rear guard, a front finger guard, high-carbon high-chrome four-edged blades and the CSA-approved panel with a 600 V transformer. Pneumatic sheet supports with return-to-front, conveyors and longer arms are options.

Ball-transfer front tables, a squaring arm with scale and front support arms are standard; the back gauge carries support fingers and the cut strip drops onto the rear slide. A pneumatic sheet support that holds the piece during the cut and returns it to the front, a conveyor for strips and longer front arms are options for thin, large or finished sheet.

A 10 ft shear needs about 16 × 10 ft of floor with the back gauge travel; a 20 ft DAS about 27 × 12 ft. 600 V 3-phase with the supplied transformer or 480 V; the motors run from 15 to 60 HP. We lay the machine out for your building before you order.

faq.q: What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?
faq.a: Finger guards along the blade, rear guard fences or photocells / light curtains, an anti-repeat single-stroke control and a mobile foot pedal with emergency stop are standard or available on every line; we recommend the photocell or light-curtain rear guard on every powered shear. In Ontario a new shear needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
